# Split host-edge and container orchestrator task authority

## Context

Native sub of neomjs/neo-agent-brain#90. The parity stack now has a container orchestrator, but the maintainer machine still runs `npm run ai:orchestrator` from the host checkout as the effective Agent OS supervisor. The intended end state is one machine with two explicit authorities:

- a **host edge** for capabilities that intrinsically touch the local desktop/session, such as wake delivery; and
- the **container plane** for cloud-capable Agent OS services and maintenance work.

This is not a request to turn off local capabilities. It is the contract that makes stopping the legacy mixed-responsibility host supervisor safe.

## Problem

Live audit at `dev@65092deb422cec749e5817937a351b106cb27d79` on 2026-07-30 found the resident host orchestrator running from the canonical maintainer checkout. Its persisted state lists 24 owned entries. It currently supervises Chroma, the bridge/wake daemon, dev server, Neural Link bridge, embed/message daemons, summary, Memory Summary backfill, KB sync, GitHub Workflow sync, backup, graph-log compaction, primary-dev sync, dream, message-concept harvest, Golden Path, two liveness watchdogs, and other scheduled work.

At the same time, `ai/deploy/docker-compose.dev.yml` defines a container orchestrator with `NEO_AI_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=cloud`. Docker was not running during the audit, so that topology owned none of this machine's work. Stopping the host process today would immediately stop its Chroma child and wake daemon, and would remove the only observed owner for multiple cloud-capable lanes.

The current binary `orchestrator.deploymentMode = local | cloud` is too coarse for the desired topology. `local` enables both machine-local edges and plane work; `cloud` disables local-only edges. Setting the host to either value cannot express “wake locally, maintain the plane in Docker.”

## Architectural reality

- `ai/configBase.mjs` owns deployment selection and the `orchestrator.localOnly` / `cloudOnly` descriptors under ADR 0019.
- `ai/daemons/orchestrator/Orchestrator.mjs` owns continuous child supervision and scheduled task dispatch.
- `ai/daemons/orchestrator/taskDefinitions.mjs` and the task registry own scheduled task definitions, but continuous children are not represented by that same classification surface.
- ADR 0014 keeps wake delivery local because it must address local harness sessions. That does not make Chroma, summary, dream, graph compaction, or watchdogs host-local.
- neomjs/neo#11720 established the earlier `cloud-deployable` / `local-only` / `shared primitive` classification direction; neomjs/neo#11503 and neomjs/neo#11519 established cross-daemon heavy-maintenance single-owner leases. This leaf consumes those precedents instead of inventing another scheduler.
- ADR 0019 forbids leaf consumers from re-reading env, duplicating legal-mode predicates, or mutating runtime config. Role/authority must be resolved once through AiConfig and consumed at the task start boundary.

## Fix — one coherent PR

Introduce an explicit orchestrator authority profile that can represent the host-edge role separately from the container-plane role. Classify every continuous child and scheduled task at its canonical definition, then derive start eligibility from that classification through AiConfig.

The host-edge profile starts only capabilities whose effects require the host/session boundary. The container-plane profile owns every cloud-capable Agent OS service or maintenance lane. Shared primitives have one declared owner per profile; they are not started opportunistically by both.

Add a startup/preflight receipt that reports the resolved owner of every task and rejects an incomplete or double-owned required lane before either supervisor begins work. Preserve the existing heavy-maintenance lease as runtime collision defense; do not mistake it for an authority model.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Source of authority | Required behavior | Failure mode / fallback | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Orchestrator role/profile | `AiConfig.orchestrator` + ADR 0019 | Resolve host-edge vs container-plane once at entry | Unknown role fails boot; no hidden `local` fallback | Config unit matrix |
| Continuous children | `Orchestrator.mjs` canonical child registry | Every child declares one authority class | Unclassified child fails the ownership audit | Exhaustive registry test |
| Scheduled tasks | task definitions / registry | Every task declares one authority class | Missing or contradictory class fails boot | Exhaustive task matrix |
| Wake delivery | ADR 0014 local delivery edge | Host edge remains capable of delivering local wakes | Container must never claim desktop wake effects | Negative container test + host positive test |
| Plane work | parity/cloud topology | Cloud-capable services and maintenance run in Docker | Host edge must not silently retain them | Resolved-owner receipt + integration test |
| Collision safety | neomjs/neo#11503 / neomjs/neo#11519 heavy-maintenance lease | Existing runtime lease remains defense in depth | Lease contention is visible, never normal routing | Existing lease regressions |

## Decision Record impact

**ADR 0019 amendment required.** Record the authority-profile leaf and profile matrix; keep the reactive Provider as the only runtime source of truth.

**ADR 0014 aligned.** Wake remains host-local; this ticket makes that exception explicit instead of using it to justify a mixed supervisor.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A canonical classification covers every continuous orchestrator child and every scheduled task; an unclassified addition fails a focused test.
- [ ] A host-edge profile starts wake/session-local effects but does not start Chroma, MC/KB plane drains, summary, dream, graph compaction, concept harvest, plane watchdogs, or other cloud-capable maintenance.
- [ ] A container-plane profile starts the cloud-capable set and never attempts local desktop wake delivery, local worktree mutation, or host-only UI/process effects.
- [ ] The combined host-edge + container-plane matrix has exactly one owner for every required lane; duplicates and gaps fail before work starts.
- [ ] The resolved ownership receipt is machine-readable and lists role, task, authority class, and effective owner without secrets.
- [ ] Existing heavy-maintenance lease behavior and local-only/cloud-only tests remain green.
- [ ] ADR 0019 records the profile/leaf contract and explicitly forbids per-consumer env or mode re-derivation.

## Out of scope

- Starting Docker or cutting over this machine (downstream dogfood leaf).
- Removing stdio support.
- Containerizing Fleet Manager.
- Changing deployment defaults merely to shrink Compose env (owned by neomjs/neo#16039 after this authority is explicit).
- Replacing the task scheduler or heavy-maintenance lease.

## Avoided traps

- **`local` renamed to `edge`:** keeps the mixed ownership while changing vocabulary.
- **Set the host to `cloud`:** disables the very local wake edge the host must retain.
- **Mutex as routing:** prevents simultaneous heavy work but cannot prove the right supervisor owns it.
- **Two classification tables:** continuous children and scheduled tasks must consume one authority vocabulary, not drift independently.
- **Per-task env flags:** recreates the env-override surface neomjs/neo#16039 exists to remove.

Supersedes the two earlier shapes on this branch. Both were caught by guards
that predate this work, and both corrections came from @neo-opus-grace.

WHAT THE FIX IS

`kbSync` and `temporal-summary` reclassify host-edge -> container-plane, and
their enable leaves move `localOnly` -> `cloudOnly` so the default resolves
enabled on the role that now owns them.

ADR-0014 §2.1 classed both local-only because they scan the Neo repo's own
corpus "from the local checkout". True when written, and its premise expired:
the non-dockerized local Agent OS was retired deliberately. The checkout did
not disappear, it MOVED -- the container is built from the repo and carries
learn/ (4.3M), src/ (5.7M), resources/content/ (168.7M) and .git (89M),
measured in the running container. Not §5.2's anti-pattern: tenant content
stays with `tenant-repo-sync` on its own GitMirror primitive.

WHAT I GOT WRONG TWICE, AND WHAT THE GUARDS SAID

1. Removing both keys from `hostEdgeProfile`'s closure. `ParityPlaneVolume-
   Scoping` pins that key set as "the graphless closure". The refutation was
   inside the list: CHROMA_DAEMON and EMBED_DAEMON are container-plane too and
   have always been listed. The closure declares what a GRAPHLESS process must
   not start -- a capability claim, not an ownership one -- so it survives any
   reclassification. Both keys restored.

2. Pinning the enablement in docker-compose instead of moving the leaves.
   `mcpHealthcheck.spec.mjs:379` refuses a production compose that sets
   NEO_ORCHESTRATOR_KB_SYNC_ENABLED: "duplicates an AiConfig default". Compose
   must inherit, so the default has to be right. Reverted; the leaf move is
   the correct change and its cost is real.

THAT COST, MEASURED

`kbSync` is the canonical "schedulable heavy lane" across the orchestrator
fixtures, so flipping its default group inverts it for every local-mode case
using it as a stand-in. Against a clean-`dev` control: 13 specs. Paid rather
than dodged -- one shared fixture line (`savedCloudOnly` already existed),
the two localOnly-mechanics specs re-based onto `primaryDevSyncEnabled`
(still localOnly, mutates a working tree), and #16166's authority spec
updated on BOTH sides.

Both sides on purpose: a reclassification that only removes a lane from one
role leaves it owned by nobody, which is this ticket's own defect and is
invisible from either role alone. Line 307 asserted the container does NOT
schedule kbSync and never surfaced -- the earlier assertion failed first and
blinded it.

New coverage for the property the whole change rests on: `cloudOnly` + null
resolves the OPPOSITE way (cloud enables, local opts in). Ownership and
enablement are separate axes and no ownership spec can see that one.

EVIDENCE

`npm run test-unit` -- the command CI runs, not a directory I picked:
  clean dev  : 5 failed / 11552 passed
  this branch: 5 failed / 11556 passed
Identical failure sets; zero regressions attributable here. The 5 are
pre-existing and order-dependent.

ADR-0014 carries a dated amendment recording why the leaves live in
`cloudOnly`, why compose stays silent, why the closure keeps both keys, and
a revalidation trigger for the container-as-checkout premise.

- 2026-08-05T17:05:50Z @tobiu referenced in commit `37e5f54` - "fix(ai): the corpus lanes move to the plane that can run them (#16554) (#16556)

* fix(ai): the corpus lanes move to the plane that can run them (#16554)

The Knowledge Base held 0 documents because nothing was producing. `kbSync`
is its sanctioned producer per ADR-0027 (the KB is deliberately outside the
autonomous recovery target set: "Knowledge Base rebuilds from source"), and
`kbSync` had never run once.

Two roles were both declining it. The container plane logged, every boot:

    Not running 5 lane(s) this role does not own — host-edge owns
    githubWorkflowSync, kbSync, primary-dev-sync, swarm-heartbeat,
    temporal-summary.

while `ai/deploy/hostEdgeProfile.mjs` declared the same five "lanes this
topology does not elect for the host edge". Five for five, exactly. Neither
statement is wrong on its own, and `auditAuthorityTopology` passed
throughout — correctly, because it audits CLASS ownership and enablement is
a different axis. Nothing compared the two.

ADR-0014 §2.1 classed `kbSync` and `temporal-summary` local-only because
they scan the Neo repo's own corpus "from the local checkout". That was
true, and its premise expired: the non-dockerized local Agent OS was retired
deliberately, so no local checkout runs a scheduler. The checkout did not
disappear, it MOVED — the container is built from the repo and carries
learn/ (4.3M), src/ (5.7M), resources/content/ (168.7M) and .git (89M) at
the built revision, which is every source both lanes read. Measured in the
running container before the change.

Not ADR-0014 §5.2's anti-pattern. That forbids re-pointing `kbSync` at
TENANT content, which stays with `tenant-repo-sync` on its own GitMirror
primitive. This changes where the Neo-corpus scan RUNS, not what it reads.

`primary-dev-sync` stays host-edge: it mutates a working tree, a genuine
host effect. `githubWorkflowSync` and `swarm-heartbeat` stay host-edge and
deliberately disabled — CI owns corpus publication, and the Stop hook makes
heartbeat redundant.

The enable leaves move `localOnly` → `cloudOnly` so `null` resolves to the
deployment default on the role that now owns them; env names unchanged. The
parity snapshot records the move in this commit, as its lint requires.

The spec is two-sided on purpose: owned-and-active on one role is half the
property. The other half is that the declining role names a DIFFERENT owner
— a lane whose decliner names itself is the shape that cost the corpus.
RED-proven: reverting the class fails the ownership spec.

ADR-0014 carries a dated amendment with its own revalidation trigger, since
the container-as-checkout premise is as mortal as the one it replaced.

1153 orchestrator specs pass.

Co-Authored-By: Tobias Uhlig <tobiasuhlig78@gmail.com>

* test(ai): the decliner-names-a-different-owner guard cannot go vacuous (#16554)

Found in review by @neo-opus-vega. `onEdge.scheduled` was length-asserted;
`onEdge.disabled` was not, so the loop carrying the load-bearing half —
"the declining role names a DIFFERENT owner" — silently stops asserting
anything if the partition ever returns an empty disabled set.

That is this PR's own defect class reproduced inside its own guard: a check
that passes because it never ran. The positive control was applied to the
posture-fragment absence assertions and missed on the more important half.

RED-proven: making `partitionRegistryByAuthority` drop non-owned descriptors
instead of collecting them now fails the spec. Before this line it passed.

Also records what actually enables the lanes, which is not in the class map.
`cloudOnly` + `leaf(null)` resolves through `resolveCloudOnlyDefault`, and
`NEO_AI_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` is UNSET on the container plane — so enablement
rests on `deploymentMode`'s own leaf default being 'cloud'
(`configBase.mjs:920`, verified against the live container). Setting that
variable explicitly to a non-cloud value takes both corpus lanes dark again,
silently, with every ownership gate green. It is a property of the
resolution chain rather than of the classification, so no spec on the class
map can see it — it belongs in the ADR's revalidation trigger, which now
carries it as its third condition.

Co-Authored-By: Vega <neo-claude-opus@neomjs.com>
Co-Authored-By: Tobias Uhlig <tobiasuhlig78@gmail.com>

* test(ai): the config-template shape pin follows the leaves it pins (#16554)

`unit` went red at e75fc952f3. `config.template.spec.mjs` asserts
`Config.orchestrator.localOnly` with an exhaustive `toEqual`, and moving
`kbSyncEnabled` + `temporalSummaryEnabled` to `cloudOnly` left two keys
asserted where they no longer live.

The test was right and did exactly its job. Updated to match rather than
relaxed to `toMatchObject`: a shape pin that cannot notice a moved or
newly-defaulted leaf is worthless precisely on leaves whose default decides
whether a lane runs at all. The comment now records that this assertion is
what caught the move.

Both leaves are additionally asserted under `cloudOnly`, where `null`
resolves the OPPOSITE way — cloud enables, local opts in — so the move is
pinned at its destination and not merely absent from its origin.

My miss: I reported `1153 orchestrator specs pass` after running
test/playwright/unit/ai/daemons/orchestrator/. True, and scoped to where I
had been editing rather than to what I had changed. A config-leaf move is
cross-cutting; its blast radius is the config surface, not the directory the
code lives in.

Verified at this head: 8872 passed across test/playwright/unit/ai/ (11.8m),
zero failures.

Unrelated and NOT introduced here, confirmed by stashing this edit and
reproducing clean: config.template.spec.mjs:287 fails on
`useUnitTestDatabase` when that file is run in isolation or under `-g`. It
passes in full-suite ordering, so it is an order-dependent isolation
artefact rather than a defect in this change.

Verified at this head: 8872 passed across test/playwright/unit/ai/ (11.8m),
zero failures.

Unrelated and NOT introduced here, confirmed by stashing this edit and
reproducing clean: config.template.spec.mjs:287 fails on
`useUnitTestDatabase` when that file is run in isolation or under `-g`. It
passes in full-suite ordering, so it is an order-dependent isolation
artefact rather than a defect in this change.

* fix(ai): the corpus lanes move to the plane that can run them (#16554)

Supersedes the two earlier shapes on this branch. Both were caught by guards
that predate this work, and both corrections came from @neo-opus-grace.

WHAT THE FIX IS

`kbSync` and `temporal-summary` reclassify host-edge -> container-plane, and
their enable leaves move `localOnly` -> `cloudOnly` so the default resolves
enabled on the role that now owns them.

ADR-0014 §2.1 classed both local-only because they scan the Neo repo's own
corpus "from the local checkout". True when written, and its premise expired:
the non-dockerized local Agent OS was retired deliberately. The checkout did
not disappear, it MOVED -- the container is built from the repo and carries
learn/ (4.3M), src/ (5.7M), resources/content/ (168.7M) and .git (89M),
measured in the running container. Not §5.2's anti-pattern: tenant content
stays with `tenant-repo-sync` on its own GitMirror primitive.

WHAT I GOT WRONG TWICE, AND WHAT THE GUARDS SAID

1. Removing both keys from `hostEdgeProfile`'s closure. `ParityPlaneVolume-
   Scoping` pins that key set as "the graphless closure". The refutation was
   inside the list: CHROMA_DAEMON and EMBED_DAEMON are container-plane too and
   have always been listed. The closure declares what a GRAPHLESS process must
   not start -- a capability claim, not an ownership one -- so it survives any
   reclassification. Both keys restored.

2. Pinning the enablement in docker-compose instead of moving the leaves.
   `mcpHealthcheck.spec.mjs:379` refuses a production compose that sets
   NEO_ORCHESTRATOR_KB_SYNC_ENABLED: "duplicates an AiConfig default". Compose
   must inherit, so the default has to be right. Reverted; the leaf move is
   the correct change and its cost is real.

THAT COST, MEASURED

`kbSync` is the canonical "schedulable heavy lane" across the orchestrator
fixtures, so flipping its default group inverts it for every local-mode case
using it as a stand-in. Against a clean-`dev` control: 13 specs. Paid rather
than dodged -- one shared fixture line (`savedCloudOnly` already existed),
the two localOnly-mechanics specs re-based onto `primaryDevSyncEnabled`
(still localOnly, mutates a working tree), and #16166's authority spec
updated on BOTH sides.

Both sides on purpose: a reclassification that only removes a lane from one
role leaves it owned by nobody, which is this ticket's own defect and is
invisible from either role alone. Line 307 asserted the container does NOT
schedule kbSync and never surfaced -- the earlier assertion failed first and
blinded it.

New coverage for the property the whole change rests on: `cloudOnly` + null
resolves the OPPOSITE way (cloud enables, local opts in). Ownership and
enablement are separate axes and no ownership spec can see that one.

EVIDENCE

`npm run test-unit` -- the command CI runs, not a directory I picked:
  clean dev  : 5 failed / 11552 passed
  this branch: 5 failed / 11556 passed
Identical failure sets; zero regressions attributable here. The 5 are
pre-existing and order-dependent.

ADR-0014 carries a dated amendment recording why the leaves live in
`cloudOnly`, why compose stays silent, why the closure keeps both keys, and
a revalidation trigger for the container-as-checkout premise.
